questions.stem: The nurse is teaching about HIV transmission. Which statement by the client is correct?

options.text: "HIV can spread through sharing needles or through unprotected sex."
"I can get HIV from hugging someone."

rationale.correct: HIV is transmitted through blood, sexual fluids, birth and breastfeeding, not casual contact.

perOption.a: HIV spreads through blood, semen, vaginal fluids and breast milk.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client with HIV has had an undetectable viral load for over 6 months on antiretroviral therapy. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: "If I stay undetectable, I won't pass HIV to my partner through sex."
"I'm cured and can stop my medicine."
"I no longer need follow-up blood tests."

rationale.correct: Daily ART keeps the virus suppressed; U=U applies to sexual transmission.

perOption.a: Undetectable = untransmittable (U=U) for sexual transmission with sustained viral suppression.
perOption.b: Stopping ART lets the virus rebound.
perOption.d: U=U applies to sexual transmission; sharing needles is still unsafe.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach about viral suppression and transmission.

questions.stem: A client with HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. Which prescription should the nurse expect?

rationale.correct: CD4 below 200: AIDS diagnosis and PCP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX.

perOption.a: A CD4 count below 200 means AIDS and a risk of PCP.
perOption.d: Live vaccines are avoided with severe immunosuppression.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Anticipate prophylaxis for a low CD4 count.

questions.stem: A client starting HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) asks about follow-up. What should the nurse tell the client?

options.text: "You'll need an HIV test before starting and about every 3 months while on PrEP."
"No testing is needed once you start."
"PrEP protects against all sexually transmitted infections."
"You only need to take it after sex."

rationale.correct: PrEP: daily (or long-acting) medication, HIV and STI testing every 3 months and kidney monitoring.

perOption.a: Regular testing makes sure HIV isn't treated with PrEP alone and checks kidney function.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: A nurse is stuck with a used needle from a client with HIV. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Wash the site with soap and water
Squeeze the wound and apply bleach
Wait until the end of the shift to report it

rationale.correct: Needlestick: wash, report right away and start PEP as soon as possible (within 72 hours, ideally within 2).

perOption.a: Immediate cleaning reduces exposure; then report it and get evaluated for post-exposure prophylaxis.
perOption.b: Squeezing and caustic agents aren't recommended.
perOption.c: PEP works best when started within hours.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: A client is starting antiretroviral therapy. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll take my medicines at the same time every day."
"I'll skip doses on days I feel well."
"I'll tell my provider before taking any new medicines or supplements."

rationale.correct: ART adherence prevents resistance and keeps the virus suppressed.

perOption.a: Consistent timing maintains drug levels.

questions.stem: A client with advanced HIV is being discharged. Which symptoms should the client report as possible opportunistic infections? Select all that apply.

options.text: A cough that lasts more than a week

rationale.correct: Report fever, cough, thrush, vision changes, diarrhea, headache and weight loss.

perOption.a: Persistent fever may mean infection.
perOption.b: This may suggest TB or PCP.
perOption.e: This may suggest an opportunistic GI infection.
perOption.f: This isn't a sign of infection.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client with rheumatoid arthritis is starting weekly methotrexate. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll take my folic acid as prescribed."
"I'll take the methotrexate every day so it works faster."

rationale.correct: Methotrexate for RA: once weekly, folic acid, no alcohol, contraception and monitoring of the CBC and liver tests.

perOption.a: Folic acid reduces side effects.
perOption.b: Taking it daily by mistake has caused fatal toxicity; it is a weekly dose.

questions.stem: A client takes tacrolimus after a kidney transplant. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.text: "Avoid grapefruit and keep your appointments for blood levels."
"Stop the medication if you feel well."
"Take it only when you have a fever."

rationale.correct: Calcineurin inhibitors: nephrotoxicity, infection risk, drug interactions and lifelong adherence.

perOption.a: Grapefruit raises tacrolimus levels; levels must be monitored.

questions.stem: A client who had anaphylaxis to penicillin is prescribed cefazolin before surgery. What should the nurse do?

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking doxycycline?

options.text: "Avoid taking it with dairy or antacids, protect yourself from the sun, and stay upright for 30 minutes after taking it."

rationale.correct: Tetracyclines: no dairy or antacids, photosensitivity, upright after dosing, avoid in pregnancy and young children.

perOption.a: Calcium reduces absorption, it causes photosensitivity and it can irritate the esophagus.

questions.stem: A client has localized herpes zoster (shingles). Which staff member should not be assigned to this client?

options.text: A pregnant nurse who has never had chickenpox or the varicella vaccine
A nurse who had chickenpox as a child
A nurse who received the varicella vaccine
A nurse who had shingles last year

rationale.correct: Shingles can spread varicella to non-immune people; cover the lesions. Disseminated zoster needs airborne and contact precautions.

perOption.a: A person who isn't immune can catch varicella from contact with the lesions.

questions.stem: A week after hiking, a client has an expanding red rash with central clearing at the site of a tick bite. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Lyme disease: erythema migrans, then possible joint, nerve and heart involvement. Treat with doxycycline.

perOption.a: Erythema migrans is the hallmark of early Lyme disease.
perOption.b: This doesn't follow a tick bite this way.
perOption.c: Cellulitis is usually warm and tender, without central clearing.
perOption.d: Shingles follows a nerve path with blisters.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: When should the nurse draw a trough level for a client receiving IV vancomycin?

options.text: Just before the next scheduled dose

rationale.correct: Trough: just before the next dose. Peak: after distribution, based on the drug.

perOption.a: The trough is the lowest level, right before the next dose.
